title: Impact of Bond Downgrade on Equity CAR

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Event‐study methodology.  
Why: A bond rating downgrade is an exogenous, precisely‐timed corporate news shock. By comparing each stock’s realised return with its own expected (normal) return in a narrow window around the announcement, we difference out all time-invariant firm factors and prevailing market movements, isolating the downgrade’s causal impact.  

Key assumptions  
1. No confounding news in the (small) event window (clean event).  
2. The market model estimated in the pre-event (estimation) window captures “normal” returns; its parameters remain valid during the event window (parameter stability).  
3. Efficient markets: any impact of the downgrade is impounded in returns immediately (hence window [-1,+1] or [-2,+2] suffices).  

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load packages
library(dplyr)
library(broom)

#--------------------------
# 1. Read the data
#--------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s56_data.csv")

#--------------------------
# 2. Set windows
#--------------------------
est_window   <- -10:-2          # estimation window for normal returns
event_window <- -1:1            # main event window
rob_window   <- -2:2            # robustness event window

#--------------------------
# 3. Estimate market model parameters per stock
#--------------------------
mm_par <- df %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% est_window) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  do(tidy(lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = .))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  select(stock_id, term, estimate) %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = estimate) %>% 
  rename(alpha_hat = `(Intercept)`,
         beta_hat  = mkt_ret)

#--------------------------
# 4. Merge parameters back and compute abnormal returns (AR)
#--------------------------
df_ar <- df %>% 
  left_join(mm_par, by = "stock_id") %>% 
  mutate(ar = ret - (alpha_hat + beta_hat * mkt_ret),         # market‐model AR
         ar_simple = ret - mkt_ret)                           # market‐adjusted AR

#--------------------------
# 5. Compute CARs
#--------------------------
car_tbl <- df_ar %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% event_window) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise( CAR   = sum(ar),
             CAR_s = sum(ar_simple) )

car_tbl_rob <- df_ar %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% rob_window) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise( CAR_rob   = sum(ar),
             CARs_rob  = sum(ar_simple) )

#--------------------------
# 6. Portfolio-average CAR and tests
#--------------------------
main_mean  <- mean(car_tbl$CAR)
t_main     <- t.test(car_tbl$CAR)$statistic
p_main     <- t.test(car_tbl$CAR)$p.value

rob_mean   <- mean(car_tbl_rob$CAR_rob)
p_rob      <- t.test(car_tbl_rob$CAR_rob)$p.value

simp_mean  <- mean(car_tbl$CAR_s)
p_simp     <- t.test(car_tbl$CAR_s)$p.value

#--------------------------
# 7. Print clear numerical results
#--------------------------
cat("=== Main result (Market model, CAR[-1,+1]) ===\n")
cat("Average CAR:", round(main_mean*100, 2), "%\n")
cat("t-stat      :", round(t_main, 2), "  p-value:", round(p_main,4), "\n\n")

cat("=== Robustness 1: Wider window CAR[-2,+2] ===\n")
cat("Average CAR:", round(rob_mean*100, 2), "%  p-value:", round(p_rob,4), "\n\n")

cat("=== Robustness 2: Simple market-adjusted returns ===\n")
cat("Average CAR:", round(simp_mean*100, 2), "%  p-value:", round(p_simp,4), "\n")
```

Running the script will output three numbers of interest:  
1. Mean CAR using the market model in the (-1,+1) window, with t-statistic and p-value.  
2. Mean CAR in a wider (-2,+2) window.  
3. Mean CAR using the simpler market-adjusted method.

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Negative. Bond downgrades signal higher default risk and tighter financing conditions; equity holders bear these costs.  
Magnitude: For US-style markets, prior literature finds roughly −2 % to −4 % over (-1,+1). Given the modest sample, I expect an average CAR of about −3 % with a t-statistic around −2 (p ≈ 0.04), and a slightly larger (≈ −4 %) effect over (-2,+2).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare equity CAR before and after bond downgrades.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: A bond credit rating downgrade leads to a positive change in equity CAR.
